title: Employment and growth
summary: [[gdp|GDP]] growth and the [[employment-report]] show how strongly an economy is running. Read together with [[inflation]], they shape what traders expect a central bank to do next.
unreliableWhen: When early figures are later revised, when parts of a report disagree (for example jobs added vs. the unemployment rate), or when one noisy month is read as a trend.
goodExample: A learner reads fictional Westmark's GDP, jobs and inflation together, notes that all three point the same way, and writes two plausible reactions with a reason for each.
badExample: A learner reacts to a single weak GDP headline without noticing that the previous quarter was revised up, so growth over two quarters was about as expected.
